key_insight: RetiJev directly scores predefined answers, outperforming larger baselines on ophthalmic guideline grading while avoiding autoregressive generation.
clinical_relevance: Fast, locally deployable decision models could support ophthalmic workflows, but clinical benefit and deployment safety remain unestablished.
method: Built source-grounded questions from PubMed Central articles, a 531-eye-disease MeSH vocabulary, and 11 grading systems.
Developed 0.8B–9B models that score candidate answers without generating reasoning text.
Compared accuracy and inference speed with a 27B LLM and Jev 1.13.
evidence_signal: The corpus contains 128,232 questions plus a 24,662-question evaluation benchmark; reported guideline-grading gains were 10.4–23.0 points, and RetiJev-9B answered a case in 158 ms on one GPU.
watch_item: Benchmark performance does not establish real-world clinical safety; predefined answer choices and deployment-specific privacy safeguards require validation.
paper_title: RetiJev: Fast and Source-Grounded Ophthalmic Decision Models
